newsitem.title: JAPAN: Rudolf Wolff says cuts back Tokyo operations.
newsitem.headline: Rudolf Wolff says cuts back Tokyo operations.

text.p: U.K.-based metals broker Rudolf Wolff has restructured its Tokyo office and moved some of its dealing operations to London, a spokesman said on Wednesday.

The spokesman for the broker declined to comment specifically, however, on a report in the Japanese business daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun that two dealers were let go last month and a third would soon resign.
The report said the restructuring was due to a drop in business with Sumitomo Corp since June, when the Japanese trade house announced massive copper trading losses.
The spokesman did not comment on Wolff's transactions with Sumitomo, although he said that since the scandal broke, many trade houses "are busy looking at their volumes of business".
He added that the restructuring involved operations such as order-taking from customers that could be handled in London.
"In this day and age a lot of business is done directly in the market," he said.
Wolff still has "a core team here that is maintaining contacts, marketing and meeting with clients", he added.
The spokesman also said Wolff had no results to announce yet from its internal investigation of dealings between its Tokyo office and Sumitomo.
On July 2, Wolff announced the suspension of three Tokyo-based employees who were cooperating with the internal investigation.

On June 13 Sumitomo announced huge losses from copper trading. It raised the estimated losses on September 19 to $2.6 billion from $1.8 billion and blamed them on unauthorised trades by dismissed copper trader Yasuo Hamanaka.
